headline: Revenue and margins grow; one-off charge causes GAAP loss
summary_short: Viatris reported Q2 2026 revenue of $3.76B (+4.9% y/y) with adjusted EBITDA of $1.19B (+10.2%) and adjusted EPS of $0.69 (+11.3%), while a $177.8M non-cash Tyrvaya impairment drove a GAAP net loss of $118.8M and diluted loss per share of $0.10.
summary_long: Total revenue rose 4.9% y/y (3.5% operationally) to $3.76B, led by Developed Markets new-product sales and 21% reported growth in Greater China; Generics growth was partly offset by ARV supply constraints in Emerging Markets. GAAP net loss widened to $118.8M, driven by a $177.8M non-cash impairment on the divested Tyrvaya product rights, not operating deterioration — operating income was positive at $6.3M and adjusted EBITDA rose 10.2% to $1.19B. The company repaid ~$900M of maturing debt, refinanced with €650M of 2033 notes, and returned ~$550M to shareholders (incl. ~$270M buybacks), cutting gross leverage to 2.9x. Viatris raised FY2026 revenue, adjusted EBITDA, adjusted EPS, and free-cash-flow guidance midpoints.

drivers.explanation: Management framed the quarter as strong execution, citing pipeline progress and early benefits of the enterprise-wide strategic review; strong first-half results supported raising full-year guidance.
Growth driven by new-product sales in Developed Markets and 21% growth in Greater China; Generics growth was partly offset by ARV supply constraints in Emerging Markets.
GAAP gross margin expanded to 38.8% from 37.2%, consistent with the same Greater China / new-launch mix shift cited for the revenue gain.
SG&A included the $177.8M Tyrvaya impairment charge, and net litigation settlements swung from a $47.6M credit to a $73.2M charge y/y.
Loss was primarily driven by the non-cash $177.8M impairment tied to the planned sale of Tyrvaya product rights, with no comparable prior-year charge.
Diluted loss per share mirrors the net loss, driven by the same Tyrvaya-related impairment charge.
Growth reflects continued operational execution and early benefits of the enterprise-wide strategic review, per management commentary.
Company repaid ~$900M of debt maturing in June, refinancing part of it with new €650M 2033 notes, lowering the gross leverage ratio to 2.9x.
Y/y increase reflects note-issuance proceeds and operating cash generation; cash also fell sharply q/q as ~$900M went to debt repayment and ~$550M to shareholder returns.
